sentences.text:
The present petition is filed by the de facto complainant in SC No.604/2024 on the files of Additional Sessions Court (Adhoc)-II, Kozhikode, seeking further investigation in the said case.
2.
The accused in the said case has been chargesheeted by the Kakkur Police for the commission of offences under Sections 354D(1)(i), 366, 450, 376(2)(n), 496, 406 and 420 IPC.
3. The allegation against the accused is that he indulged in sexual relationship with the de facto complainant by giving false promise of marriage to her.

It is also alleged that a farce marriage was performed at the instance of the accused, at the premises of a temple on 20.3.2018, to make the de facto complainant believe that the accused is her lawfully wedded husband.
There is also the allegation that the accused had siphoned off gold ornaments and cash from the de facto complainant.
4. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that the investigation carried out by the Kakkur Police was not at all satisfactory.
According to the petitioner, the Investigating Agency did not question the 1st wife of the accused, and failed to incorporate the offence under Section 493 IPC in the Final Report.
It is for the above reason that the 2025:KER:66556       3 petitioner/ de facto complainant seeks further investigation in this case.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
6.

The prayer of the petitioner to have further investigation conducted in this case in respect of the offence under Section 493 IPC, is prima facie unsustainable in law in view of the provisions contained in Section 198 Cr.P.C.

As per the aforesaid provision, no court is empowered to take cognizance of an offence punishable under Chapter XX of Indian Penal Code, except upon a complaint made by some person aggrieved by the offence.

Thus, if the Investigating Agency submits a further report incorporating the offence under Section 493 IPC, the court concerned will not be in a position to take cognizance upon such further report in connection with the commission of the aforesaid offence.
Therefore, the prayer of the petitioner in the present petition is prima facie, not maintainable in law.
The petition is accordingly dismissed.
